title: Field runbook update + blocker digest (Feb 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a concise field-facing runbook update plus a digest of active customer blockers from the past two weeks (Feb 12–26, 2026). Intended audience: field eng, SRE on-call, solutions engineering handoff. Use this when triaging live installs or prepping for customer calls.

Quick summary: 
- Two high-priority customer installs with persistent network pathing issues (B2B-regulated and fintech pilot).
- One on-prem thermal/ops blocker (hardware vendor integration) causing delayed KV cache performance verification.
- Updated verification steps to the VPC preflight checklist and added 2 new troubleshooting commands for NAT/GW asymmetry.
- Action items assigned; ETA estimates listed below.

Attendees (notes taken by Priya):
- Priya Sharma (owner)
- Marco Alvarez (field eng)
- Janelle Kim (solutions eng)
- Samir Gupta (infra integration)
- Evan Brooks (SRE oncall)

Agenda:
1) Blocker rollup (customer-by-customer)
2) Runbook changes to preflight & post-install checks
3) Short-term mitigations and owners
4) Questions for vendor/partner teams

Blockers (detailed):
1) AcmeHealth (regulated healthcare, on-prem appliance) — SEVERITY: P1 -> P0 candidate
- Symptom: Intermittent TLS handshake failures between private control plane and customer gateway during heavy token uploads (spikes at >700 rps).
- Observed: Retries accumulate at the connection layer; KV cache priming fails intermittently causing 200–400ms tail latency spikes in local inference.
- Temporary workaround: Route control-plane traffic via fallback peering (us-east-1 -> us-east-2) and throttle bursts from the ingestion worker to 400 rps.
- Root hypotheses: MTU mismatch or a firewall deep packet inspection (DPI) device resetting connections under payload signature.
- Actions:
  * Marco to coordinate packet captures with customer (PCAP) and provide sanitized dump to network team (owner: Marco) — ETA 2026-03-03.
  * Samir to validate TLS cipher compatibility and confirm latest control-plane cert chain (owner: Samir) — ETA 2026-02-28.
  * Priya to schedule vendor DPI escalation if packet traces show resets (owner: Priya) — ETA 2026-03-05.
- Linked ticket: PD-987 (see linked_artifacts)

2) MeridianFin (fintech pilot, VPC peering) — SEVERITY: P2
- Symptom: Cross-account VPC route propagation intermittently drops routes after BGP flaps at customer edge. Observed loss of model artifact access for 3–5 minutes.
- Observed: BGP session resets correlate with predictable backup network maintenance windows on customer's side.
- Temporary workaround: Implemented 60s backoff + retry at artifact fetch layer so small flaps don't impact live requests.
- Actions: 
  * Janelle to deliver artifact fetch retry PR with exponential backoff parameterized by env var; target merge to staging by 2026-03-01 (PR #58 linked).
  * Evan to add SLO alerting for artifact fetch failures > 30s and runbook step for reverting fetch cadence (owner: Evan) — ETA 2026-03-04.
- Notes: Customer ops flagged this as acceptable for pilot if retries are robust; consider longer-term: prewarming artifact caches in the VPC.

3) EdgeCorp (on-prem, thermal throttling) — SEVERITY: P2
- Symptom: GPU frequency scaling during long seq workloads causes KV cache writes to slow, failing some load tests.
- Observed: Hardware vendor's firmware older than recommended; telemetry shows frequent thermal events when running continuous batching.
- Temporary workaround: Lowered max batch size and enabled aggressive pad-and-flush cadence to reduce sustained utilization peaks.
- Actions: 
  * Field eng to verify vendor firmware update schedule and coordinate maintenance window (owner: Marco + EdgeCorp infra) — ETA 2026-03-12.
  * Add explicit firmware version check to preflight and block install if older than recommended (owner: Priya) — incorporated below in runbook changes.

Runbook changes (applied 2026-02-26):- VPC preflight additions:
  * new step: verify NAT gateway asymmetry (run: /scripts/check-nat-asymmetry.sh) — returns non-zero if egress IPs differ across AZs.
  * new check: control-plane TLS cipher/chain validation command: /scripts/verify-control-tls.sh --host <control-host>
  * firmware gating: install abort if GPU firmware < 3.4.1 (vendor baseline) — message: "FW_TOO_OLD" and guidance doc link.
- Post-install verification: 
  * artifact fetch warmup: attempt artifact pull from all configured S3 endpoints with 3 retries and 10s jitter; record timings to install.log
  * KV cache sanity check: run mini-load test (1000 tokens @ 50 qps) and verify median token latency < 25ms

New troubleshooting snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- check-nat-asymmetry.sh (usage):
  1) ssh to bastion
  2) run: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/check-nat-asymmetry.sh --az all
  Expected: single egress IP per AZ. If different, see NAT config note below.

- verify-control-tls.sh (usage):
  sudo /opt/redwood/bin/verify-control-tls.sh --host control.redwood.example.com --port 443
  Output: JSON-ish text (sanitized for support) with cipher list and cert chain fingerprint. If TLS mismatch, escalate to Samir.

Customer handoff checklist (for SE -> Field Eng):
- Confirm capture: PCAP or sanitized flow logs present in /tmp/handovers/<customer>-pcap.zip
- Confirm runbook version: runbook_version in install.log == 2026-02-26-v2
- Confirm artifact warmup latencies < 3s per artifact
- Ensure ticket annotated with relevant Slack links and oncall rotations

Decisions made in this meeting:
- Short-term: prefer control-plane routing fallback to different region over risky firewall changes at customer side.
- Medium-term: add firmware gating into install pipeline (accepted).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are customers willing to accept a 60s artifact fetch backoff for critical production? MeridianFin agreed for pilot, but need formal approval for prod. (owner: Janelle)
- Should we auto-rotate peering on BGP flaps or only provide notifications? Tradeoff: faster failover vs complex automation. (owner: Priya to write proposal)
- Need clarity from infra on whether DPI devices can be configured to avoid resetting TLS when payloads look like model CKPTs (owner: Samir).

Notes to self (quick, messy):
- Collect one sanitized PCAP sample with timestamps aligned to retry spikes. Remove payloads before uploading to Jira.
- Re-check that new preflight scripts have <= 5s runtime on small VM; anything longer delays install gating.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marco: capture PCAP for AcmeHealth + upload sanitized to PD-987 — 2026-03-03
- Samir: confirm TLS chain + document any cert mismatch steps — 2026-02-28
- Janelle: finalize artifact-fetch retry PR and coordinate staging deploy — 2026-03-01
- Evan: add artifact-fetch SLO alerts and runbook step — 2026-03-04
- Priya: add firmware gating to install pipeline + update Confluence runbook page — 2026-03-08

Retrospective notes (short):
- Good: quicker diagnosis on MeridianFin due to earlier instrumentation of artifact timings.
- Improve: need clearer expectations with customers about maintenance windows impacting BGP; add this to onboarding checklist.

References / quick links: PD-987 (AcmeHealth network), PKG-1423 (installer improvements), PR#58 (artifact retry).

If you're on-call and hit one of these symptoms: follow the Customer handoff checklist, then run the two checks (check-nat-asymmetry.sh and verify-control-tls.sh). If results are non-zero, create a labeled incident with tags: private-deploy, network, pcap_required and ping field-eng.

-- end of digest --

(Internal note: this doc should be copied into Confluence after owners confirm action ETAs; leave in Drive as the working draft.)
